hardware.variant: One assembled kit with operator-reported CoreBoard V1.2.

inputs.name: Ordinary ESP_MOSAICO_SC101IOT kernel used after the U-Boot splash

scenario: In one RAM-only boot, the operator ran the published optional U-Boot command mosaicosplash red. Without resetting the board, the ordinary EmberBSD kernel booted and LVGL was started.
expected: The U-Boot diagnostic shows a red field; after the same boot enters EmberBSD and starts LVGL, framebuffer output remains visible.
observed: The operator confirmed a solid red field from U-Boot. After kernel boot and LVGL start in the same boot, the operator confirmed the display became fully black. The kernel attached espspi0 → spi0 → cofb0. Post-init CO5300 reads were id=ff:ff:ff, power=ff, format=ff and brightness=ff, each with error=0. After LVGL, cofb0 reported rows_changed=960, rows_sent=960, errors=0 and last_error=0. The post-refresh SPI snapshot was clkrst=00800043, gate=00000003, cmd=00000000, ctrl=003c0000, clock=80000000, user=08002040, user1=00400000, user2=00000000, misc=0000003e and int_raw=00001000.
limits: One assembled V1.2 sample; this was a RAM-only sequence and did not write NOR.
The confirmed red U-Boot field establishes visible output before kernel boot on this sample; it does not establish EmberBSD display acceptance.
The row counters report framebuffer-driver transfer completion only. They do not establish panel command acceptance or switched-supply voltage.
CO5300 values of 0xff with error=0 are not a validated panel identity or acknowledgement.

The post-refresh snapshot showed CTRL=0x003c0000 and USER=0x08002040. The published U-Boot four-line transmit path programs CTRL=0x003c8000 (idle-high plus bit 15) together with USER.FWRITE_QUAD. The snapshot was taken after framebuffer activity, not during a transfer; this discrepancy is diagnostic evidence, not proof of cause or panel acceptance.
An earlier GPIO-bit-banged trial also remained black and did not support status reads. No physical rail voltage was measured.
